ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a distribution map of sea-level isobars, marked with 120°E, 150°E, and 30°S, indicating that this region is located in the Southern Hemisphere. Place 1 is located in the upper-middle part of the figure, and the nearby isobars are roughly distributed in a curved manner; from the isobar values, there is a relatively high-pressure area on the southwest side of place 1, such as the side of 1024 hPa, while the pressure near the northeast side is relatively lower, such as the side of 1016 hPa. Then reason: The pressure gradient force points from high pressure to low pressure, so near place 1 it roughly points from southwest to northeast. Since this place is located in the Southern Hemisphere, when near-surface wind moves toward low pressure under the action of the pressure gradient force, it will be affected by the geostrophic deflection force and deflect to the left, and the actual wind direction is roughly blowing toward the northwest. Wind direction is named according to the direction it comes from, so wind blowing toward the northwest comes from the southeast, that is, southeast wind.
